introduction: On this Sunday, Amos says he was only a herdsman when the Lord took him and said, Go, prophesy. In the Gospel, Jesus sends out the Twelve two by two, with nothing for the journey but a staff. Paul gives thanks that God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. Let us hear the Lord's call to us, and go where he sends us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may travel light and trust in the Lord as she proclaims the Gospel. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries and all who go out two by two to share the faith: that they may be welcomed and protected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who think they are too ordinary to serve God: that they may hear his call, as Amos did. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick: that the Church may anoint them and bring them Christ's healing. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live for the praise of God's glory, who chose us in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you chose us in Christ before the world began. Send us out as your witnesses, and give us confidence in your care. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Sent out two by two
reflection.body:
Amos was not a professional prophet. When the priest at Bethel tells him to go away and prophesy somewhere else, Amos answers: "I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son, but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs; and the LORD took me from following the flock." God called an ordinary working man and gave him a message.

In the Gospel, Jesus sends the Twelve on their first mission. He sends them "two by two," so that no one goes alone. And he tells them to take almost nothing: "no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse." They are to depend on God and on the hospitality of the people they meet. If they are not welcomed, they are to move on. They go out, preach repentance, cast out demons, and anoint the sick with oil.

This is a picture of the Church's mission in every age. We are sent together, not as lone heroes. We are sent with little, so that people see God's power and not our own resources. And the mission includes care for the sick: the anointing in this passage is one of the roots of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.

Paul's letter to the Ephesians opens with a hymn of praise. God "has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world." Before we did anything, we were chosen and loved.

You do not need to be a professional to be sent. Like Amos, God takes us from our ordinary work. This week, think of one person you could share your faith with, or one sick person you could visit. Go with a friend if you can, and travel light.
